For a new Next.js SaaS in 2026, the right authentication pick is almost always Better Auth or Supabase Auth.

## Key Options

**Better Auth**
Better Auth is a TypeScript-native library that owns your users in your own Postgres with first-class multi-tenancy. It runs in your app and stores users in your database, launched in 2024 and reached v1.6 in May 2026. It features the most complete feature set — 2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation, and more with no vendor lock-in and a plugin system.

**Clerk**
Clerk is a hosted authentication service where you add their SDK, get production-quality sign-in screens and user management out of the box, and pay per monthly active user—the fastest path to a working sign-in form and the slowest to scale a cost-controlled business on top of. Clerk's standout features in 2026 are organization management (multi-tenant apps) and impersonation, handling the entire user-to-organization mapping with a few lines of configuration.

**Auth.js (NextAuth v5)**
NextAuth, now officially called Auth.js v5, is the original Next.js auth library with the same package (next-auth) and same maintainers. It is OAuth-focused with adapters for major databases and is mostly relevant today for apps that already run on it.

## Performance & Recent Developments

Better Auth is fastest because its checks are direct database queries with no external API call, typically completing in under 5ms in production. 

On July 7, 2026, Vercel announced it was acquiring Better Auth, with the Better Auth core team joining Vercel to work on Agent Auth, an identity layer built for AI agents.

Choose better-auth for new self-hosted TypeScript apps, Clerk when authentication is a product surface you want to outsource, and NextAuth v5 when you are already deep in the Next.js and Auth.js ecosystem.

# Better Auth Basic Usage Guide

## Server Configuration

Enable email/password authentication by configuring the auth instance:

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"

export const auth = betterAuth({
    emailAndPassword: {
        enabled: true,
        autoSignIn: true // defaults to true
    }
})
```

**Database Setup**: The documentation mentions requiring a database adapter but doesn't provide specific SQLite/Kysely configuration details in this section. You'll need to reference the full integration docs for adapter setup.

## Client Authentication Methods

### Sign Up
```ts
const { data, error } = await authClient.signUp.email({
    email,
    password, // minimum 8 characters
    name,
    image, // optional
    callbackURL: "/dashboard" // optional
})
```

### Sign In
```ts
const { data, error } = await authClient.signIn.email({
    email,
    password,
    callbackURL: "/dashboard",
    rememberMe: false
})
```

### Sign Out
```ts
await authClient.signOut({
    fetchOptions: {
        onSuccess: () => router.push("/login")
    }
})
```

## Session Management

### Client-Side with Hook
```ts
const { data: session, isPending, error } = authClient.useSession()
```

### Server-Side Access
Pass request headers to retrieve session data:
```ts
const session = await auth.api.getSession({
    headers: await headers()
})
```

**Note**: "Always invoke client methods from the client side. Don't call them from the server."

# Configuring Better Auth with SQLite and better-sqlite3

## Setup

To integrate Better Auth with SQLite using the better-sqlite3 driver, install the dependency and configure it in your auth file:

```ts title="auth.ts"
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import Database from "better-sqlite3";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: new Database("database.sqlite"),
});
```

According to the documentation, better-sqlite3 is described as "the most popular and stable SQLite driver for Node.js."

## Database Migrations

The Better Auth CLI streamlines schema management. Run migrations using your preferred package manager:

**npm:**
```bash
npx auth@latest migrate
```

**pnpm:**
```bash
pnpm dlx auth@latest migrate
```

**yarn:**
```bash
yarn dlx auth@latest migrate
```

**bun:**
```bash
bun x auth@latest migrate
```

The documentation confirms that SQLite supports both schema generation and migration operations through the CLI, enabling you to "generate or migrate your database schema based on your Better Auth configuration and plugins."

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about Next.js 16's proxy.ts replacing middleware.ts for route protection:

## Key Changes

proxy.ts replaces middleware.ts and makes the app's network boundary explicit. In Next.js 16, proxy.ts replaces middleware.ts. It runs on every request before your routes render, making it perfect for session refresh and route protection.

## Migration Steps

Rename middleware.ts → proxy.ts and rename the exported function to proxy. Logic stays the same. Alternatively, you can run npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy to automate the migration.

## Important: Silent Breaking Changes

**Critical warning:** A leftover middleware.ts is ignored at build time with no error, so auth/redirect logic stops executing and protected routes become publicly reachable. This means if you upgrade to Next.js 16 without renaming your middleware.ts file, route protection will silently stop working without any build warnings.

## Why This Change?

Clearer naming and a single, predictable runtime for request interception. The move from Middleware to Proxy in Next.js 16 is more than a filename change. proxy.ts makes the request boundary clearer: redirects, rewrites, headers, cookies, and early responses belong there only when they genuinely need request‑time context.

## Deprecation Status

The middleware.ts file is still available for Edge runtime use cases, but it is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

--- title: Next.js 16 description: Next.js 16 includes Cache Components, stable Turbopack, file system caching, React Compiler support, smarter routing, new caching APIs, and React 19.2 features. url: "https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16" docs_index: /docs/llms.txt publishedAt: October 21st 2025 authors: - Jimmy Lai - Josh Story - Sebastian Markbåge - Tim Neutkens --- Ahead of our upcoming [Next.js Conf 2025](https://nextjs.org/conf), Next.js 16 is now available. This release provides the latest improvements to Turbopack, caching, and the Next.js architecture. Since the previous beta release, we added several new features and improvements: - [**Cache Components**](/blog/next-16#cache-components): New model using Partial Pre-Rendering (PPR) and use cache for instant navigation. - [**Next.js Devtools MCP**](/blog/next-16#nextjs-devtools-mcp): Model Context Protocol integration for improved debugging and workflow. - [**Proxy**](/blog/next-16#proxyts-formerly-middlewarets): Middleware replaced by `proxy.ts` to clarify network boundary. - [**DX**](/blog/next-16#logging-improvements): Improved logging for builds and development requests. For reminder, those features were available since the previous beta release: - [**Turbopack (stable)**](#turbopack-stable): Default bundler for all apps with up to 5-10x faster Fast Refresh, and 2-5x faster builds - [**Turbopack File System Caching (beta)**](#turbopack-file-system-caching-beta): Even faster startup and compile times for the largest apps - [**React Compiler Support (stable)**](#react-compiler-support-stable): Built-in integration for automatic memoization - [**Build Adapters API (alpha)**](#build-adapters-api-alpha): Create custom adapters to modify the build process - [**Enhanced Routing**](#enhanced-routing-and-navigation): Optimized navigations and prefetching with layout deduplication and incremental prefetching - [**Improved Caching APIs**](#improved-caching-apis): New `updateTag()` and refined `revalidateTag()` - [**React 19.2**](#react-192-and-canary-features): View Transitions, `useEffectEvent()`, `` - [**Breaking Changes**](#breaking-changes-and-other-updates): Async params, `next/image` defaults, and more Upgrade to Next.js 16: ```bash filename="terminal" # Use the automated upgrade CLI npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest # ...or upgrade manually npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest # ...or start a new project npx create-next-app@latest ``` For cases where the codemod can't fully migrate your code, please read the [upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). ## New Features and Improvements ### Cache Components Cache Components are a new set of features designed to make caching in Next.js both more explicit, and more flexible. They center around the new `"use cache"` directive, which can be used to cache pages, components, and functions, and which leverages the compiler to automatically generate cache keys wherever it’s used. Unlike the implicit caching found in previous versions of the App Router, caching with Cache Components is entirely opt-in. All dynamic code in any page, layout, or API route is executed at request time by default, giving Next.js an out-of-the-box experience that’s better aligned with what developers expect from a full-stack application framework. Cache Components also complete the story of Partial Prerendering (PPR), which was first introduced in 2023. Prior to PPR, Next.js had to choose whether to render each URL statically or dynamically; there was no middle ground. **Choice: Better Auth**, over Auth.js v5 and Clerk. As of 2026, Auth.js is in maintenance mode (security patches only, original maintainer left, Vercel acquired Better Auth in July and is folding its team into Vercel's identity work). Clerk is hosted/per-MAU billing — fine if you want to outsource the whole surface, but it means an external service holding your user data and a recurring cost. Better Auth is self-hosted, TypeScript-native, stores users in your own DB, and is what the ecosystem now points new Next.js projects to.

**What's implemented:**
- `src/lib/db.ts` / `src/lib/auth.ts` — SQLite (`better-sqlite3`) + Better Auth server instance, email/password + Google OAuth enabled
- `src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` — auth API routes
- `src/lib/auth-client.ts` — client hooks (`signIn`, `signUp`, `signOut`, `useSession`)
- `src/app/sign-in/` — combined sign-in/sign-up form + Google button
- `src/proxy.ts` — Next.js 16's `proxy.ts` (replaces `middleware.ts`), guards `/dashboard`, redirects to `/sign-in` if no session
- `src/lib/users.ts` — rewired to read from Better Auth's own `user` table instead of the hardcoded array; `getCurrentUser()` now reflects the real session
- Sign-out button on the dashboard, sign-in/dashboard links on the homepage
- `.env.example` with placeholders for `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`
